title: Zari (metallic and imitation thread)
subtitle: Metallic yarn, imitation (copper/brass) zari and a little real silver/gold zari
covers: This page covers zari thread makers. Zari is an input for weaving (borders, brocades) and embroidery, so it feeds those pages rather than sitting in a straight line.

snapshot.text: Surat is called India's zari capital: about 55-70% of India's zari production by different sources; about 800 registered units (association) or more than 15,700 units (TOI). Counts differ widely.
Real silver and gold zari has shrunk as metal prices rose; metallic yarn (from metallised polyester film) and imitation copper/brass zari now make up most output.
Surat zari has a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, received in Nov 2010 (as reported by IANS).

items.text: Zari is decorative metallic thread. It was once made of gold and silver; today most is copper or brass wire electroplated to look like gold or silver, or metallic yarn made from metallised polyester film.

sections.title: Sub-segments, and which one this page covers

cells: About 50% (one industry CEO); about 80% with imitation (association)
Under 10% silver; gold only on special order

sections.title: Where it sits in the value chain

stages.label: Copper / brass wire, polyester film, silver

items.text: Handloom weavers in other states (Banarasi, Kanjivaram) use Surat-made threads.

blocks.note: General description. Confirm on a site visit.

steps.d: Copper/brass wire is drawn and flattened, or polyester film is metallised and slit.
Flattened wire or film is wrapped around a core thread.
Imitation zari is electroplated to a gold or silver look.
Thread wound on reels for weavers and embroiderers.

items.text: Surat produces more than 600 tonnes a month of copper and brass zari wire (one industry CEO).
CPCB's White list includes zari work done by hand.
Electroplating is a chemical process and is likely treated differently from hand zari work. Ask for the GPCB consent; the category was not confirmed.
About 1,05,000 artisans are directly employed and 50,000 indirectly; many are migrants from Bihar earning Rs 7,000-9,000 a month, often seasonally.

sections.title: Fragility points and early warning signs for a lender

items.text: Metal price swings: gold rose from Rs 42,758 (2021) to Rs 1,48,465 per 10 g (Mar 2026), pushing real zari to a niche.
Inventory of copper or silver can lose value quickly; check how much metal stock the unit carries and whether it is hedged.
Demand depends on the wedding and festival season for sarees and lehengas.
Cheque returns or frequent overdraws; cash credit used near the limit all month.
Electricity units falling month on month, or a shift stopped, without a matching fall in loan outstanding.
Creditor days stretching; suppliers charging late-payment interest; purchases switched to cash from new sources.
Stock or receivables building up; sales concentrated on one or two parties or brokers.
Wages paid late or labour leaving; regular weekly closures.
New borrowing from private lenders or related parties; machines rented out or sold.
